There is very little they can do - http://smallbusiness.chron.com/need-trademark-clothing-lines-24186.html

Copyright doesn't cover clothing at all. That's why they use their logos, which are trademarked. As far as I know, you can't trademark something that isn't actually a trademark - e.g. a picture you chose to use on some shirt once.

A huge company like Disney can own the rights to Mickey Mouse on clothing because it's protected under copyright for its use in movies, books, etc. It's not an image that only exists on clothing. Obviously this works well for something very distinct, like a cartoon character. However, it doesn't work for something that would otherwise be too generic to be copyrightable or that wasn't already copyrighted as part of a work that is copyrightable, (book, movie, magazine, whatever).
